stories.headline: Iran-Israel war LIVE: UAE’s image as West Asian haven tested by Iran war Iran Israel war LIVE updates: Trump postpones Iran attack after developments in talks
stories.summary: Iran and Israel are engaged in a escalating conflict, with Iran warning the US to accept its latest peace proposal to maintain a fragile ceasefire. The UAE has denied a report of a visit by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, as the country's image as a West Asian haven is tested. Pakistan's prime minister has invited delegations from Iran and the US to Islamabad for talks on Friday, following a proposed two-week ceasefire to allow for diplomacy. Meanwhile, Iran has retaliated against Israel with over 300 ballistic missiles. The US has considered a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and former US President Trump has postponed a planned attack on Iran amid developments in talks. The situation remains volatile, with life in the region in limbo amidst ongoing tensions and conflict.

stories.headline: International partners draw red line on Somalia’s one-sided path to elections
stories.summary: Somalia's Federal Government has begun a disputed one-year mandate extension, delaying elections until 2027. International partners are attempting to prevent a constitutional and political crisis. The UN mission welcomed recent discussions between May 13 and 15, praising international partners for their support, but expressed regret that no breakthrough was reached. The extension has raised concerns among Somalia's international donors, who are drawing a red line on the government's one-sided approach to elections. Puntland and other regions are affected by the decision, which may exacerbate existing political tensions. The international community is urging Somalia to find a more inclusive and democratic path forward, with the UN and other partners working to avert a deeper crisis. The situation remains unresolved, with further negotiations and developments expected.

stories.headline: Indonesia’s oil hub plan collides with Asean’s trust deficit
stories.summary: Indonesia's Energy Minister, Bahlil Lahadalia, proposed hosting an ASEAN oil storage hub to strengthen regional fuel reserves and improve energy security. The idea was announced at the 48th ASEAN Summit in Cebu, with Lahadalia stating that such a hub would help supply Southeast Asia during future disruptions. The proposal aims to address energy security concerns amid ongoing Middle East tensions. However, the plan's success may be hindered by ASEAN's trust deficit and lack of unity. Indonesia's President has expressed support for stronger ASEAN food and energy resilience, and the country is pushing for the oil hub to enhance regional cooperation and stability. The proposal is part of broader discussions among Southeast Asian countries to improve energy security and reduce reliance on external sources.

stories.headline: Anwar vows no cuts to sports funding as athlete welfare made national priority
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has assured that sports programmes and athlete welfare will not be affected by budget cuts due to the global economic crisis. He stated that there will be no cuts to sports funding, despite financial constraints. Anwar made this announcement during the National Sports Award, emphasizing that sporting events, activities, and athlete welfare will continue to be fully protected. This decision prioritizes athlete welfare as a national concern, safeguarding sports development and infrastructure. The Prime Minister's assurance aims to alleviate concerns among athletes and the sports community, ensuring that Malaysia's sports sector remains unaffected by the current economic challenges.

stories.headline: Google Translate marks 20 years, processes 1 trillion words monthly
stories.summary: Google Translate has marked 20 years of service, processing approximately 1 trillion words monthly. The platform now supports nearly 250 languages and serves over 1 billion users monthly, covering 95% of the world's population. Recent upgrades have focused on making translations more natural and conversational, utilizing Google's latest AI systems, including Gemini models. The tool has evolved from a 2006 experimental project in Google Research laboratories to a global communication platform, offering features like live translation, speech recognition, and real-time cross-cultural communication. A new pronunciation practice tool has also been introduced on Android. Google Translate's growth reflects its significant role in everyday communication, travel, and language learning, with its AI-powered features continuing to enhance user experience. The platform's development is a testament to the advancements in machine learning and AI technology over the past two decades.

stories.headline: Google I/O 2026: What to expect, when and how to watch the tech event
stories.summary: Google's annual developer conference, I/O 2026, kicks off on May 19th. The event will be livestreamed, allowing the public to watch announcements and updates on various Google products and services. Expected highlights include updates on Gemini, Android XR, and other Android-related news. The keynote will be available to watch live on Google's platform. Attendees and viewers can expect exciting news from various facets of Google's ecosystem. The event will be covered live from Mountain View, with updates available online. Those interested in watching from home can tune in to the livestream, which will provide real-time access to the conference's announcements and presentations. The conference is a significant event for developers and Android enthusiasts, offering insights into Google's latest developments and future plans.

stories.headline: Malicious code found planted on users' PCs
stories.summary: A Steam game has been found to contain malicious code, sparking controversy. The malware is hidden within a DLL file that loads when the game is executed, attempting to steal users' sensitive information. This discovery is the latest in a series of malware-related incidents, including a recent attack that mimics a Windows update to trick users into executing malicious commands. The malware is written in JavaScript, making it relatively easy to analyze, and appears to be limited to manipulating files such as .zshrc, .bashrc, and a temporary text file. Users are being urged to exercise caution and avoid executing suspicious commands or downloading unverified software to protect themselves from such threats. The incident highlights the ongoing risk of malware and the importance of robust security measures to prevent and detect malicious code.

stories.headline: addlink previews new lineup of memory solutions through online showcase
stories.summary: Addlink has concluded its 2026 virtual showcase, focusing on memory and storage solutions for AI systems, gaming rigs, and creator workflows. The company introduced its new S93 drive, the latest addition to its NVMe SSD lineup. The virtual showcase highlighted addlink's latest storage and memory solutions for various applications, including AI PCs, gaming systems, and everyday digital workflows. As a global storage and memory solution provider, addlink aims to cater to diverse needs with its innovative products. The company had previously announced its virtual showcase for 2022, which featured its AddGame SPIDER X5 DDR5 RGB Memory Line-up. Further information on addlink's products and solutions is expected to be released, with the company being a notable player in the industry, also partnering with prominent brands. Addlink's storage and memory solutions are designed to enhance performance and efficiency.

stories.headline: D-Day in Spygate - what happens next? Southampton's place in the play-off final is at stake as they face a disciplinary hearing as they stand charged of watching a Middlesbrough training session.
stories.summary: Southampton faces a disciplinary hearing for spying on a Middlesbrough training session, putting their place in the play-off final at stake. The English Football League (EFL) charged the Saints, who have pleaded guilty. An independent panel will conduct the hearing, expected to take place on or before Tuesday, May 19. The result is anticipated to be announced on Tuesday. Possible sanctions from the disciplinary commission include expulsion from the play-offs or a substantial fine. The incident occurred during the semi-final against Middlesbrough, and the EFL released a statement confirming the hearing schedule. The outcome will determine Southampton's fate in the play-off final, with a decision expected shortly. The club's actions have been deemed a breach of EFL regulations, leading to the disciplinary proceedings.

stories.headline: 'We're here solely to play football,' insists North Korean coach before Asian Champions League semi-final SUWON: The coach of the first North Korean sports team to visit the South in eight years batted away questions Tuesday (May 19) about the prospect of South Kore
stories.summary: The North Korean women's football team, Naegohyang Women's FC, has arrived in South Korea for the Asian Women's Champions League semi-final. This marks the first visit by North Korean athletes to the South in eight years. The team will face Suwon FC Women on May 20. The coach of Naegohyang Women's FC stated that they are "here solely to play football," deflecting questions about the broader implications of their visit. The team's arrival on Sunday was the first time South Korea has received North Korean athletes in over seven years. A list of 27 players and staff from Pyongyang was sent ahead of the visit. The Asian Women's Champions League semi-final match is scheduled to take place in Suwon.

stories.headline: "Our cherished son's meningitis developed too rapidly to stop it" Tommy was sleeping with his mum watching over him when he suddenly started having a seizure.
stories.summary: A five-month-old baby, Tommy, died from meningitis that developed rapidly. He was sleeping with his mother when he suddenly had a seizure. Despite being watched over, the meningitis progressed too quickly to be stopped. In memory of his son, Tommy's father ran for three days to honor him. The baby's condition deteriorated rapidly, and unfortunately, it was not possible to save him. The father's run is a tribute to his "cherished" son, raising awareness about the rapid onset of meningitis. The family's experience highlights the importance of recognizing the symptoms of this serious infection, which can be fatal if not treated promptly.

stories.headline: "You're really clever, aren't you?" BVB's assist king snaps at transfer-rumour questions Manchester United have made enquiries about Julian Ryerson, according to Sky.
stories.summary: Manchester United have made enquiries about signing Julian Ryerson, according to Sky. The Norwegian player, currently under contract with Borussia Dortmund until 2028, has been the subject of transfer speculation. When questioned about potential transfers, Ryerson responded sarcastically, "You're really clever, aren't you?" implying he knows no more than the reporters. It remains unclear if Manchester United's interest will lead to a concrete offer. If a transfer does occur, Dortmund is expected to demand a fee of at least €30 million. The outcome depends on several factors, and Ryerson's future with the club is still uncertain. Ryerson has also denied rumors of interest from Barcelona, stating "you know more than I do." The situation will continue to unfold as the transfer window progresses.

stories.headline: United States clears $428 million Apache, M777 support package for India
stories.summary: The United States has approved two military support packages for India worth $428 million. The packages cover sustainment support for AH-64E Apache attack helicopters and M777A2 ultra-light howitzers. The proposed support will enhance India's ability to address current and future threats, strengthen homeland defense capabilities, and deter regional threats. The deals, cleared by the US Department of State, are part of the Foreign Military Sales program. The support packages aim to deepen defense ties between the US and India, boosting their strategic and military cooperation. The approval includes services for Boeing AH-64 Apache attack helicopters and will help India maintain its defense capabilities. The total value of the approved packages is estimated at $428.2 million.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Refuses To Modify Directions To Remove Stray Dogs From Public Places
stories.summary: The Supreme Court refused to modify its earlier directions to remove stray dogs from public places, citing rising dog bite cases, especially against children and older people. The court reiterated its stance on the issue, stating that stray dogs pose a threat to public health. The order, issued on November 7, 2025, directed all states and union territories to ensure the removal of stray dogs from high-footfall public institutions, including educational institutions, hospitals, and highways. The court dismissed petitions against the order, making it clear that it will not modify its earlier directions on shifting stray dogs from public areas, including schools, hospitals, and other institutional areas. The decision aims to protect public health and safety, particularly in areas with high human traffic.

stories.headline: Delhi High Court Sends Lawyer-YouTuber To Jail For Criminal Contempt After 'Taanashahi' Remark Against Judiciary
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has sentenced a lawyer and YouTuber, Gulshan Pahuja, to jail for criminal contempt. Pahuja, who runs the channel "Fight 4 Judicial Reforms," made scandalous comments about the judiciary, including a remark referring to the judiciary as "Taanashahi," which translates to dictatorship. The court initiated suo motu proceedings against Pahuja, finding him liable for criminal contempt. The judgment was delivered on April 22, with the court taking a strong stance against Pahuja's comments, which were deemed derogatory and undermining the authority of the judiciary. Pahuja's channel advocates for judicial reforms, but his comments crossed the line, leading to the contempt charge and subsequent jail sentence. The case highlights the court's efforts to maintain its dignity and authority.

stories.headline: 'Provided Rs 50,000 regularly': Mother-in-law counters dowry allegations in Twisha Sharma death case
stories.summary: Retired judge Giribala Singh, the mother-in-law of deceased model and actress Twisha Sharma, has submitted online transaction records in court to counter dowry harassment allegations. The records show transactions ranging from Rs 5,000 to Rs 50,000, which she claims were regularly provided to Twisha. Giribala Singh stated that Twisha's death is a major loss for the family. She also claimed that Twisha was taking schizophrenic medication and would often resist taking her medicines, saying "don't monitor me" and "don't force me". The mother-in-law's statements aim to refute allegations of dowry harassment in Twisha Sharma's death case. The court is considering the evidence presented by Giribala Singh in response to the dowry allegations.

stories.headline: China stocks wobble as bond concerns, geopolitics weigh on sentiment China stocks ​struggled for direction on Tuesday, while Hong ​Kong shares rose as ‌investors assessed the ​impact of the U.S.-China summit outcomes and the globe
stories.summary: China stocks struggled for direction on Tuesday, amid concerns over bond markets and geopolitics. The uncertainty follows the recent U.S.-China summit, with investors assessing the outcomes. Hong Kong shares, however, rose, indicating a divergence in market sentiment. Additionally, China's rare earth stocks declined 2.4% by midday after Australia ordered Chinese background investors to divest their holdings in a rare earths project. The move highlights escalating trade tensions between nations. Overall, China's stock market is navigating a complex environment, with global market turbulence and trade tensions contributing to the uncertainty. The rare earths project divestment order adds to the concerns, impacting investor sentiment and stock performance. As a result, China stocks are experiencing volatility, while Hong Kong shares demonstrate resilience.

stories.headline: Global geopolitics and Modi’s unrelenting war against inflation ‘Modinomics’ has been winning the war against inflation, slowly but steadfastly, no matter which metric is used as the benchmark
stories.summary: India's economic policies, known as 'Modinomics', have been successful in controlling inflation, with progress seen across various metrics. Under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the country has undergone significant economic transformation since 2014. The government's efforts have led to currency stabilization and upgrades from global rating agencies, making India the first large country to achieve this since the 2007-08 financial crisis. The World Bank and IMF have praised India's rising GDP, although some critics argue that Modi's economic policies have missed their mark in certain areas. Despite this, the data suggests that 'Modinomics' has been effective in managing inflation, with steady progress observed over time, regardless of the benchmark used to measure it. This economic paradigm has reshaped the nation, combining various policies to drive growth and stability.

stories.headline: Markets chop to geopolitics while Trump holds off on immediate Iran attack - Newsquawk US Market Wrap ZeroHedge - On a long enough timeline, the survival rate for everyone drops to zero
stories.summary: US President Trump has put on hold a planned attack on Iran, with the White House deeming Iran's updated proposal to end the conflict as "insufficient" and "TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE". The proposal was seen as Tehran surrendering to Trump's demands, according to Iranian state media. Geopolitical tensions continue to drive market price action, with oil prices rising and the US dollar index (DXY) firmer by around 0.4%. The US Senate previously voted against limiting Trump's Iran war powers. Ongoing US-Iran negotiations have yet to yield an agreement, with Trump warning that the "clock is ticking" for Iran. The situation remains uncertain, with markets reacting to mixed geopolitical headlines and higher oil prices, leading to a mostly negative tone in APAC stocks despite a positive handover from Wall Street. The US has also begun its own blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Crude Oil Futures Market - Volatility, Geopolitics, and a Battle Between Supply and Demand The crude oil futures market has entered one of its most complex periods in years. Traders are navigating a collision of geopolitical instability, uncertain dem
stories.summary: The crude oil futures market is experiencing a complex period due to geopolitical instability and a battle between supply and demand. Current market sentiment indicates a potential increase in supply, putting downward pressure on prices, with Brent crude and WTI showing slight declines. Despite a recent spike in oil prices, J.P. Morgan Global Research forecasts Brent crude to average around $60/bbl in 2026. Previously, WTI Crude climbed 12.6% to reach highs around $77.62 per barrel. The market is navigating uncertainties, including geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and China's demand. The crude oil market has retained its lead in ton-miles, increasing from 8 trillion in 1999 to over 10 trillion by 2024, with coal and oil products also showing growth. Traders are closely monitoring the market for updates on supply and demand.

stories.headline: Sensex Rises Over 300 Points, Nifty Crosses 23,700 Amid Positive Market Sentiment
stories.summary: Indian stock markets rallied with the Sensex rising over 300 points and the Nifty crossing 23,700, driven by positive market sentiment. The surge follows US President Donald Trump's announcement to halt planned military strikes on Iran, easing global tensions. Benchmark indices extended their upward momentum, with the Nifty IT index jumping over 3% to lead gains. In contrast, the Nifty Private Bank index declined over 0.7% to lead losses. On the National Stock Exchange (NSE), around 2,152 stocks advanced, indicating a broad-based rally. The market's firm and optimistic note is attributed to the positive global cues, with investors reacting positively to the de-escalation of tensions between the US and Iran. The rally has lifted investor sentiment, with the Indian equity markets opening on a strong note.

stories.headline: Sensex, Nifty end lower as banking drag offsets IT rally; rupee hits record low
stories.summary: The S&P BSE Sensex fell 114.19 points to 75,200.85, while the NSE Nifty50 declined 31.95 points to settle at its closing value. The downturn was driven by a decline in banking stocks, which offset gains in the IT sector. The Indian rupee hit a record low of 96.62 against the US dollar, pressured by rising crude oil prices and geopolitical instability, including the US-Iran deal. The currency has depreciated 1.5% this month and over 7% this year, making it Asia's worst-performing currency in 2026. Despite the broad market decline, IT stocks such as Infosys and Oracle posted strong gains, along with Realty and PSU Bank sectors showing resilience. The decline in the market was also influenced by surging bond yields, which reached all-time highs.

stories.headline: Stock Market Today: Sensex Jumps 343 Points, Nifty Crosses 23,750 As IT Stocks Lead Market Rally
stories.summary: The Indian stock market surged today, with the Sensex jumping 343 points and the Nifty crossing 23,750. The rally was led by IT stocks, amid improved market sentiment. Global crude oil prices slipped over 2% after the US decided to delay a planned strike on Iran, with Brent crude falling to $109.15 per barrel and WTI crude declining to $107.28 per barrel. The Nifty 50 traded above 23,730, while the BSE Sensex gained over 330 points in early trade. The market also saw gains in metal, chemical, oil, and gas stocks, despite mixed global cues. The Sensex ended over 1,100 points higher from its day's low, with the Nifty 50 near 23,650. The market update was reported on January 16, 2026.

stories.headline: Stock Market Today: After Monday’s Meltdown Drama, Sensex Jumps 330 Points and Nifty Cruises Higher in a Tuesday Comeback Sequel
stories.summary: Indian stock markets rebounded on Tuesday, with the Sensex jumping 330 points and the Nifty crossing 23,730 in early trade. This comeback follows a significant decline on Monday, where the Sensex crashed over 800 points and the Nifty slipped below 24,000. The recovery is largely attributed to a strong rally in IT stocks and cooling crude oil prices. The market's move higher indicates a positive shift after the previous day's meltdown. The Nifty's gain is a notable development, as it had fallen below the 24,000 mark on Monday. The rebound suggests that investors are regaining confidence, leading to a surge in stock prices. The Indian stock market's performance is closely watched, given the global economic context, including the aftermath of the COVID-19 recession that began in February 2020.

stories.headline: CenturyPly Reclaims 30% of IT Workload and Turns Operations Into a Strategic Growth Engine Using ManageEngine Solutions
stories.summary: CenturyPly has successfully reclaimed 30% of its IT workload by implementing ManageEngine solutions. The company has eliminated over 50 daily password-related help desk calls and automated the onboarding process for 70-100 employees every month. This reduction in IT support workload has enabled CenturyPly to transform its operations into a strategic growth engine. ManageEngine's AI-powered IT management has provided predictive insights, unified intelligence, and automation, allowing CenturyPly's IT team to work more efficiently. The implementation has resulted in significant improvements, including reduced help desk calls and streamlined onboarding processes. By leveraging ManageEngine's solutions, CenturyPly has been able to optimize its IT operations and focus on strategic growth initiatives. The partnership has enabled the company to run its IT operations more resiliently and efficiently.

stories.headline: What MACOM Technology Solutions Holdings (MTSI)'s AI‑Driven Revenue Guidance and Data Center Demand Means For Shareholders
stories.summary: MACOM Technology Solutions Holdings (MTSI) has released strong Q2 2026 earnings and upgraded its data center outlook, driving its shares up 160% since August. The company provides analog semiconductor solutions for wireless and wireline applications. Its Linear Drive Pluggable Optics are expected to remain central to AI-era data center buildouts, with improving margins toward long-term targets. Recent updates on MTSI stock show a positive reaction to the Q1 earnings report and upbeat guidance, reinforcing a bullish fundamental story across data center, industrial/defense, and telecom markets. The company has also released Q3 2026 earnings guidance, further solidifying its position. Accelerating AI-related demand and robust Q2 results have contributed to the surge in MTSI's shares, making it a notable player in the industry. MTSI's valuation has been impacted by these developments, reflecting its growing presence in key markets.

stories.headline: How Trump's crypto venture and Iran's top exchange tapped into the same industry networks
stories.summary: Iran's Nobitex exchange has processed at least $2.3 billion through Tron and BNB Chain blockchains since 2023. These blockchains were created by backers of the Trump family's World Liberty Financial venture, indicating a connection between the two entities. Despite international sanctions, Nobitex has been able to tap into the same industry networks as Trump's crypto venture. The data, analyzed by Reuters, reveals significant crypto transfers on Tron and BNB Chain, totaling $2.3 billion. This development highlights the complex and interconnected nature of the cryptocurrency industry, where entities with differing interests and affiliations can operate within the same networks. The transactions have raised questions about the potential implications of these connections and the flow of funds through these blockchains.

stories.headline: Travel agency cancels holidays with 200 customers warned flights 'under review'
stories.summary: AVG Travels, a Melbourne-based travel agency, has cancelled holidays for over 200 customers, citing "operational scheduling adjustments" as the reason. The agency has since gone unresponsive, leaving travellers seeking refunds and answers. This incident comes amid a wave of flight cancellations in the US, with American Airlines cancelling over 360 flights on Monday and 800 on Sunday. The US has seen over 1,000 flight cancellations daily, with 1,300 cancellations on Friday. The cancellations are causing concerns for travellers, particularly with the New Year's weekend approaching, which is expected to see a surge in air travel. Affected customers are advised to explore alternative flight options, with tools like Google Flights available to find last-minute flights and compare prices. Refund and rebooking processes remain uncertain for AVG Travels customers.

stories.headline: OpenAI avoided a costly court loss to Elon Musk, but neither side is unscathed
stories.summary: A US jury ruled against Elon Musk in his lawsuit against OpenAI, finding the company not liable. Musk had sought the ouster of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, among other changes. The jury decided Musk waited too long to sue, and his lawsuit was barred by the statute of limitations. OpenAI, valued at $852 billion, remains on track for a potential large initial public offering. The trial pitted Musk against his fellow OpenAI co-founders, with witnesses testifying in support of Altman. The verdict allows OpenAI to move forward without significant changes, while Musk's loss may impact his influence over the company. The outcome brings an end to the high-stakes trial, with neither side emerging completely unscathed. OpenAI's future plans, including its potential IPO, can now proceed without the uncertainty of the lawsuit.

stories.headline: Elon Musk loses his lawsuit against OpenAI and boss Sam Altman
stories.summary: A federal jury rejected Elon Musk's $150 billion lawsuit against OpenAI and its CEO Sam Altman. Musk had claimed that Altman and others breached their duty to OpenAI's original nonprofit mission and unjustly enriched themselves. However, the jury found that Musk waited too long to bring the claims, ruling that they were barred due to the statute of limitations. The unanimous verdict by the nine-person jury determined that OpenAI and Altman were not liable to Musk. The lawsuit was an attempt by Musk to oust Altman from his leadership position, but the jury's decision was a major blow to Musk's efforts. The verdict marked the end of the lawsuit, with the jury finding in favor of OpenAI and Altman. Musk's claims of mistreatment by his OpenAI co-founders were also dismissed.

stories.headline: Musk vs OpenAI: A courtroom clash that raises questions about the AI race
stories.summary: Elon Musk's $150 billion lawsuit against OpenAI and its CEO Sam Altman was rejected by a federal jury. Musk had accused OpenAI of prioritizing commercial gain over the public good, but the jury ruled that his claims were barred by the statute of limitations. The lawsuit was part of a larger legal battle between the two tech titans, exposing tensions over the mission and financial goals of artificial intelligence development. The case raises questions about the future of AI and the balance between profit and public benefit. Musk's loss is seen as a significant blow to his credibility and efforts to shape the AI industry. The verdict marks a major victory for OpenAI, allowing the company to continue its work on AI development without the burden of the lawsuit.

stories.headline: Jury throws out Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman
stories.summary: A federal jury in California has rejected Elon Musk's $150 billion lawsuit against OpenAI and its CEO Sam Altman. The jury found that Musk waited too long to file the lawsuit, exceeding the statute of limitations. Musk had claimed that OpenAI betrayed a shared vision to remain a nonprofit dedicated to guiding artificial intelligence development for humanity's benefit. The jury ruled that OpenAI, Altman, and co-founder Greg Brockman were not liable on all claims. The lawsuit was dismissed, with the nine-person jury unanimously determining that the claims were barred due to the statute of limitations. The decision is a significant blow to Musk's efforts, and the case has been dismissed by a federal judge in California. The verdict was reached in under two hours, indicating a clear decision by the jury.
